summary: Round 5. The round-4 major is fixed. WIRING.md now has a 'Configure before the first power-up' section, and both WIRING.md and ASSEMBLY.md have step 13 with the exact Betaflight CLI command (set motor_output_limit = 74, save) and a gate: Blackbox/OSD peak <= 60 A on a full pack. The Loads table shows the 14.22 A capped peak and names its source. The limit is described as a central estimate. The VTX antenna is on +y, with its head (z >= 48) about 3 mm above the battery plug's top (z 45), and the pigtail pre-bend / 8-10 mm heat-shrink note is in both build documents. Every check passes. The FEA hot spots are where the load path puts them (arm root screws, the body around arm_1's screws, top-plate pillar feet and the deck-to-pillar joints), and each load is applied where the real load enters. What remains is minor: some documents disagree with each other, one XT60 retention concern, and items carried from earlier rounds that need checking on the bench.

findings.issue: The 8-10 mm heat-shrink note for the XT60 pigtail is in WIRING.md, ASSEMBLY.md and DESIGN.md, but the generated BOM still lists 'heat-shrink for AWG 12 joints, 20 mm pieces' (row 35). That is the length the note says reaches the rear pillar. The turn itself is still tight: the leads pass the front stops at x -44.85 and must be at |y| >= about 12-14 by the pillar's rounded end at x -37.5..-33, which means two 90 deg bends of about 5 mm radius in 12 AWG silicone. It is buildable with the pre-bend, and the pillar's rounded ends give a little room.
findings.fix: Make the AWG 12 heat-shrink BOM row 10 mm (a bom_extra override or a per-run heat-shrink length in the wiring entry), so the shopping list matches the instruction.

findings.issue: Nothing positively stops the XT60 from pulling out rearward. The front stops take the plugging-in force, but against the 20-40 N it takes to unplug an XT60, only the cable tie's friction holds the male connector (the cradle is open at the rear). Unplugging the battery every flight can walk the connector out of the cradle and load the pigtail's solder joints at the ESC pads.
findings.fix: Add a 0.8-1 mm lip at the cradle's rear edge that clips behind the housing's mating face (the plug only needs the 8.1 x 16 mm opening), or a second tie through slots at x about -66. At the least, add a build note: hold the XT60 body when unplugging.

findings.issue: The generated ASSEMBLY.md never says to drop the 12 M3 nuts into the arm and stack nut pockets, or to tape the stack nuts, whose pockets open downward. It also puts every soldering step after the top plate, battery and strap are on. DESIGN.md has the correct order (nuts in step 2, solder in step 5 before the top plate). The source docstrings are stale: arm.py says the arm screws are M3 x 12 (BOM and fastener check: M3 x 14), and body.py says the post screws are M3 x 6 (BOM: M3 x 8).
findings.fix: Engine: for nut_trap receivers, add a 'press N nuts into <part> pockets' line before the step that drives the screws (and say so when a pocket opens downward). Let a project put the electrical steps before a named mechanical step (here, before top_plate). Fix the two docstrings.

findings.issue: Some DESIGN.md numbers no longer match report.json. Printed mass is given as 145 g (report: 149.5 g). The FEA results are given as arm 9.8, body 9.8 and top plate 7.7 / 8.7 MPa (report: 9.50, 9.61, 7.03, 8.86). Gaps carried from round 4: the XT60 has no weight_g in the catalog, so the report counts it as 0.0 g; the battery's 140 mm lead (`supplied`) and the motor phase lead gauge/length are assumed, not catalogued.
findings.fix: Update the DESIGN.md numbers. Add XT60 weight_g (about 4 g for a pair, Amass), plus the CNHL lead length/gauge and the XING2 lead gauge/length, each with a source.

findings.issue: Carried, now handled in the documents: the 14.22 A per motor under the cap is a central propeller-law estimate. With rpm falling by less than duty at part load and the full pack at 25.2 V instead of 24 V, the real peak could be about 60-66 A against the XT60's 60 A rating, which Holybro gives for 1 minute. The 5 s bursts make this physically fine, and step 13 now gates first flights on the Blackbox/OSD peak.
findings.fix: None needed beyond the documented gate. If the measured peak is over 60 A, lower motor_output_limit by 1-2 % and re-check twr (6.18 leaves about 3 % margin).

findings.issue: Carried: the single strap band sits 14.5 mm ahead of the pack's centre (x 4.5..24.5), because the VTX takes x -27.5..0.5. The rear of the pack is held only by the anti-slip pad.
findings.fix: Acceptable with the pad. If the pack shifts in testing, add a second band at about x -36, or move the VTX back.

findings.issue: Carried: at 0 deg tilt the cheek tips, and at 35-40 deg the roof tongue's front corners, may show at the edges of the camera image. Both are clear at the 25 deg home tilt.
findings.fix: Check with the camera fitted. Chamfer the cheek tips or round the roof corners if they show.

findings.issue: Carried: the first arm bending mode is about 165 Hz, in the gyro noise band, and the PETG-CF arm sits directly under a motor base that can reach 70-80 C. Both are listed in the DESIGN.md risks.
findings.fix: Hover test plus a Blackbox gyro-noise check before freestyle. Consider a 0.5-1 mm standoff ring or washer stack under each motor.
